meta.title: Russian Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 33 letters · both directions, as two cards per letter
meta.desc: The 33 letters of the Russian alphabet, in alphabetical order — the first deck of the Russian collection, since the level decks are written in Cyrillic from their first card and carry no transliteration. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Every note gives the letter in capital and small, its name (what a Russian calls it when spelling a word aloud), its sound described in English words, and one everyday word that shows it, with its stress marked and a speaker beside it. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them; where English has no near equivalent, as for ы, the rolled р and х, the card says so. Two things the spelling does not show are on the cards because a beginner meets them at once: an unstressed о is said like а, and е, ё, ю and я soften the consonant before them. The two signs, ъ and ь, have no sound of their own, and their cards say what they do instead.

fields.Name: е
fields.Sound: "ye" as in yes; after a consonant, "e" — and the consonant is softened

fields.Name: ё
fields.Sound: "yo" as in yonder; always stressed, and often printed as е

fields.Name: и кра́ткое
fields.Sound: "y" as in boy — a short и, always beside a vowel

fields.Name: эль
fields.Sound: "l" as in ball, said with the tongue low

fields.Name: о
fields.Sound: "o" as in more when stressed; unstressed, it is said like а

fields.Name: эр
fields.Sound: a rolled "r", made with the tip of the tongue; English has no equivalent

fields.Name: ха
fields.Sound: "kh", like the ch in Scottish loch

fields.Name: ша
fields.Sound: "sh" as in shop, with the tongue pulled back

fields.Name: ща
fields.Sound: a long, soft "sh", as in fresh sheep said quickly

fields.Name: твёрдый знак
fields.Sound: the hard sign: no sound of its own; it keeps a consonant apart from the е, ё, ю or я after it
fields.Example: подъе́здentrance (to a block of flats)

fields.Name: ы
fields.Sound: a vowel between the i of bit and the u of put, said with the tongue pulled back; English has no equivalent

fields.Name: мя́гкий знак
fields.Sound: the soft sign: no sound of its own; it softens the consonant before it
